archive.compression: tar (GNU tar, --format=posix, --sort=name, --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner, one fixed --mtime for every member = runner_session.json's at, pax headers without atime/ctime) | zstd -19 -T0

exports_json_seal_note: exports.json (a sealed member of the session record) names the five exports by size and sha256; those digests are the ones listed under archive.members, so the seal is verifiable after restore.

external_backup.state: the complete original directory: exactly the 16 original files, read-only; the hash list covers all 16 and sha256sum -c passed at archival

note: These hashes are an integrity anchor for the archived bytes; they do not prove the session's verdict — the verdict is re-derived by the production judge from the restored files.
restore: Fresh restore and re-judge, executable: python3 -B evidence/b3/b3_17A6_2026-10-15-03/restore_rejudge.py (from the repository root).

What it does, in order: an EMPTY temporary directory; the five members extracted; the eleven ordinary files copied; exactly sixteen files, each checked by size and sha256 against this document; the export seal; the archived manifest verified with its pins; the pinned plan and prediction verified byte-for-byte before being read; the session plan REBUILT from the authoritative inputs (the archived manifest, the pinned documents, the archived ruling's slice and disposition, the bound instrument's arithmetic) and compared to summary.json's l6; the production judge_session, equal to adjudication.json key for key; runner_session.json against the rebuilt plan and that verdict; the boundary record.
tool: archive_session.py/1.0.2 (b3 lifecycle 2, main preparation 2026-10-14; follow-ups to the owner's reviews of 0850e6b and 0a86d00)
